title: Un paraguas azul
label: ch:es-paraguas
canDo: I can deal with something I have lost: read a message describing a mislaid object by colour and by the part you hold, say that I cannot find it anywhere, and ask to be told rather than ask anyone to go looking.

payoff.summary: Read a message to the building group about a mislaid umbrella, then answer it both ways.
payoff.note: THE SIBLING CHECK, RUN ON THE CHAPTERS CITED RATHER THAN ON THIS ONE, CAUGHT FIVE DUPLICATIONS BEFORE A LINE WAS COMMITTED. That rule was filed in lessons.d during chapter 469 and this chapter is what it was written for. (1) ES-C330-parada (seq 5630) ALREADY OWNS THE WHOLE para- FAMILY: "A parasol is made ready against the sun, and a parachute ready against a fall -- that para- is the Romance parare, and not the Greek para- meaning beside that sits in parallel and parable." The draft gloss for paraguas was para ("stops") plus aguas, which would have CONTRADICTED a merged lesson outright: parare is TO MAKE READY. Cited, and roots: [parare-latin] makes paraguas a cousin of parada. (2) ES-C440-cumpleanos owns the verb-plus-noun compound that looks plural and is singular -- "the -s you can hear is the plural of anos trapped inside a word that is now singular... not an exception to be memorised; it is a sentence that hardened". Cited as the shape paraguas repeats. (3) ES-C447-analisis ALREADY NAMES el paraguas as its worked example of the invariable plural: a word already ending in s whose stress is not final takes no plural ending, like el lunes. Cited, not re-derived. (4) ES-C451-cola owns the homonym-family presentation, a table of unrelated words sharing one spelling. mango (handle, from Latin manus) versus mango (the fruit, through Portuguese manga from Malay mangga, behind it Tamil mankay) is that shape exactly, so cola is cited and only the new case is added. (5) ES-C267-no-nada (seq 2580) OWNS DOUBLE NEGATION IN FULL, including the rule that a negative word after the verb still requires no in front. The synthesis draft was restating it as new for por ninguna parte. Now cited, with the claim narrowed to what is actually new: ninguna parte joins nada, nadie and nunca as a negative word and is two words rather than one, and the trap is that English renders it with the positive-looking ANYWHERE, which pulls a learner toward en cualquier parte. THE SAME PASS IMPROVED THE CHAPTER RATHER THAN ONLY CORRECTING IT. `ls ES-C383-*.md` turned up ES-C383-dejar sitting beside ES-C383-buscar, and the exam message opens with `me he dejado un paraguas`. So the chapter has a four-verb arc with three verbs already held: dejar (left it), buscar (looking), encontrar (NEW, cannot find), avisar (NEW, let me know). encontrar therefore arrives as the missing piece of a sequence rather than as a bare word, and buscar/encontrar is taught as the effort-versus-result split English collapses into one verb. ES-C451-mostrar (seq 11860), NOT ES-C11-stem-changes, is the o-to-ue owner to cite: it is recent, prints the full stress table, and already names la rueda as the earlier sighting. encontrar -> encuentro is the same rule one chapter-group later. AVISAR IS HANDED OVER, NOT INTRODUCED. ES-C332-aviso already glosses it ("behind it is the verb avisar, to notify") and ES-C459-habitual uses it again ("lo habitual es avisar"). Same move imprimir made with el impreso in 469. roots: [latin-videre] -- PREFIX-FORM SLUG, the shape ES-C332-aviso holds, which is the thing chapter 466 got wrong. The derivation ad visum / videre belongs to aviso and is NOT repeated; what this lesson adds is what that derivation predicts, that avisar is the weakest of the telling verbs because it makes visible rather than orders, which is exactly why the message says `si lo habeis visto, avisadme` and not `buscadlo`. mango takes roots: [latin-manus], the slug ES-C24-mano holds, so the handle and the hand are cousins -- which is what the cousins join key exists for. manus itself belongs to ES-C24-mano (manual, manufacture, maintain) and is cited rather than re-derived. SAFETY: the exam message contains `o lo ha cogido alguien`. ES-C35-tomar warns that coger is coarse slang across much of Latin America, so that clause is DROPPED from the synthesis quote rather than put in a variety: general learner's mouth. Verified by grep that no lesson in this chapter contains coger in any form. One loose claim tightened before commit: a draft said the Italians named the umbrella "for sunshine". umbra is a SHADOW, so the contrast is shade against water, and the sentence now says so.
